Hi Alice —

Great to meet today — thanks for the time. Quick recap and next steps around the PII handling items you raised during the demo:  

- What gets stored: By default, Redwood persists request metadata and model inputs/outputs for 30 days for debugging and quality monitoring. We can opt out of storing prompt text and raw outputs for specific routes.
- Where it’s stored: Data for hosted accounts lives in our US regions (AWS us-west-2 / us-east-1) and is encrypted at rest (AES-256). For Dedicated/Private deployments, data stays in customer-controlled VPCs.
- Retention controls: We offer configurable retention per-route (30/90/365 days or permanent) and an API to purge data on demand.
- Logging/trace controls: You can enable structured logging without raw prompt text (token-level counts only) and redact fields via a configurable sanitation policy.
- Residency: Acme Health requested US-only residency — we can ensure all hosted logs/archives are pinned to US regions for your account.

Next steps I promised:  
1) Share an internal one-pager that maps prompts/outputs -> where stored and retention defaults (attached).  
2) Technical confirmation on whether we can disable storing raw prompt text for production routes (Aditya to confirm).  
3) Provide SOC 2 artifacts and evidence request template (attached SOC2-evidence-request.xlsx).

Can you confirm these next steps look right? If so, I’ll loop in our security lead for the technical confirmation and propose a short follow-up call.

Thanks,

Hi Alice — looping in to confirm the technical details you asked about. Short answer: yes, and a few implementation notes below.

- Compute without persistence: For routes configured with "no-persist" flag, Redwood will process the request in-memory, run model inference, return the output, and avoid writing prompt or output text to persistent storage. Temporary in-memory caches (KV cache) are used during inference but are never written to disk and are cleared after the response lifecycle.
- Generated text storage: When "no-persist" is enabled, generated text is not stored in logs, observability traces, or storage buckets. We still emit anonymized telemetry (token counts, latency, error rates) for platform health.
- Programmatic retention control: Retention is configurable both via Console and our Management API. The Management API supports per-route retention settings and a purge endpoint that can delete stored prompts/outputs and associated artifacts. Purge operations are logged in our audit events (who, what, when) and retained according to your account's audit retention policy.
- Audit logs: Audit events for purges and data-access are available and can be exported to your SIEM or S3; events include user id, operation, timestamp, route id, and originating IP.

Caveats & recommended validation:  
1) If you use features that rely on historical context (persistent KV cache or prefix caching), those features will not be available for "no-persist" routes.
2) Some platform-level backups (snapshot metadata) may contain non-identifying route metadata; we can provide a certification of what's included per-account.

If you'd like, we can provide a short test plan (1-2 calls) where Acme can exercise the no-persist flag and validate that nothing is written to your designated storage. We can also provide sample API calls for the purge endpoint.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Infra Engineer, Security & Platform
